latin: Primus septennarius uitae humanae est sub Mercurio, secundus sub Venere, tertius sub Marte, quartus sub Ioue, quintus sub Saturno, et reliqui septennarii secundum eum qui fuerit praedominatus in praecedentibus.
translation: The first seven-year period of human life is under Mercury, the second under Venus, the third under Mars, the fourth under Jupiter, the fifth under Saturn, and the remaining seven-year periods follow whichever planet has predominated among the preceding ones.
translation_note: 'septennarius' names a seven-year period of life; 'praedominatus' is rendered 'predominated,' of a planet's rule over the earlier septennia, a usage Farmer's note does not further gloss (farmer1998:22372).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch15, from Latin at farmer1998:22344
attribution: Pico's own opinion, in the doctrine of Plato (section 5>, farmer1998:22132).
doctrine: The thesis assigns each successive seven-year period of a human life to a planet in turn, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, and has later septennia follow whichever planet has predominated among the earlier ones (farmer1998:22344). Farmer treats it as part of the same set as 5>9-10 and 5>12, in which the sun and moon are read as figures for the intellect and its lower reflection in reason, and in which, he states, no predictive or horoscopal astrology is involved (farmer1998:22372).
context: The same unsigned study of Pico, Louvain, and the crisis of Renaissance astrology treats this thesis as part of the block 5>9-12 that Farmer connects to conclusion 22.4 (txt_medieval_and_early_modern_science_:1446).
historiography: Busi and Ebgi print the Latin of the thesis in their edition without independent commentary on its planetary scheme (busi2014:24610).
not_established: No external doctrinal parallel for the septennial-planetary scheme, beyond Farmer's grouping of the thesis with 5>9-10 and 5>12, is established by the sources consulted.
